summary: The bridge's Loft facts arm now consumes the CG-BINDING volume entry. `solid_volume`, `solid_local_bbox`, `top_seam_mismatch` and `loft_mesh` for `SolidSpec::Loft` first run the landed analytic line-section ruled arm (V5: bit-identical, the fast path for the class it already certifies); when that arm refuses a spline-section carrier, the new certified smooth arm reconstructs each section loop exactly (chord-length clamped cubic, component-wise — the same `Edge.make_spline` convention the landed lathe arm uses, never a flattening polygon), assembles the ruled smooth surface's tensor-Bernstein patches, and submits every patch to the sanctioned `crate::python::binding::volume_facts` entry, summing the certified brackets and adding the exact planar end-cap moments. The certified class is the two-station loft, where the smooth station interpolation is exactly determined by the recorded data (every interpolation degree reduces to the linear one across two stations) — the smooth surface IS the ruled surface, so the recorded reference is reproduced exactly. A three-or-more-station smooth spline loft's station parameterization is an OCC `ThruSections` convention the row does not record, so the arm refuses TYPED naming the open smooth carrier (`unsupported_envelope`/`non_canonical_carrier`) rather than substituting a ruled approximation (scope decision 1; the packet's stop condition). No tolerance is stretched, no recorded reference edited, and the landed line-loft verdicts are untouched. `facade.rs` and `corpus/ttc/door.py` were in the write set but required no change (the door already records spline sections and the carrier routing already reaches the facts arm).

implementation.bridge_types: truck123d/src/bd_bridge.rs: `SpanPoly3` (a 3-D power-basis cubic span); `chord_params3`; `quadratic_span3`; `spline_spans3` (the 3-D reconstruction, reusing the landed 2-D `clamped_slopes`/`hermite_power` component-wise); `cubic_bernstein` and `span3_bernstein` (exact power->Bernstein degree-3 controls); `spline_loop_spans` (a closed section loop of line/spline edges with the exact seam-closure check); `poly_integral`/`span_area_moment`/`spline_loop_area_vector` (Green's-theorem signed area vector); `spline_loop_bbox3` (exact span extrema via `cubic_roots`); `certified_spline_loft_volume` (per-patch `crate::python::binding::volume_facts` + exact caps, returns `(value, lo, hi)`); `eval_span3`/`sample_loop3`/`centroid3`/`spline_loft_mesh` (the deterministic ruled tessellation).
implementation.dispatch: `solid_volume(SolidSpec::Loft)` -> analytic `loft_sections`/`loft_volume` when it certifies, else (open chain) `certified_spline_loft_volume`; `solid_local_bbox` -> union of the two sections' exact AABBs on the fallback; `top_seam_mismatch` -> `Ok(None)` for an open spline loft and typed refusal for a closed one; `loft_mesh` -> `spline_loft_mesh` on the fallback.
implementation.refusal: `open_smooth_loft()` = `Refusal::UnsupportedEnvelope(EnvelopeCase::NonCanonicalCarrier)`, the landed mapped refusal (the door marshals it to `{"case": "unsupported_envelope", "envelope": "non_canonical_carrier"}`). Every failure path is this typed value; there is no untyped path and no approximation.
implementation.binding_consumption: The arm calls `crate::python::binding::volume_facts(&VolumeRow { numerator, weights, orientation })` — the Rust fn behind the pyo3 `binding_volume_facts` export — once per ruled patch. The numerator is the 4x2 Bernstein net `[[A_0,B_0],...,[A_3,B_3]]` of the two spans, the weights are all 1 (the exact polynomial route), and the orientation is +1; the cap terms carry the recorded-loop winding exactly as the landed line-loft arm's caps. The bridge never names `truck_geometry` and never names `TensorBernsteinPatch`.
implementation.facade: No change required. The Loft carrier is already classified `Swept`; the facts arm is reached from `bd_facts`/`bd_stl`, not the facade router.
implementation.door: No change required. `corpus/ttc/door.py`'s `loft` already records the spline-section boundary via `_wire_profile_edges` (never a flattening polygon) and the facts/STL arm is where the corpus rows stop.

findings.title: The certified smooth class is the two-station loft; the multi-station corpus rows refuse typed
findings.detail: The bridge can consume only the sanctioned facade's plain-data `VolumeRow` (one tensor-Bernstein patch); it cannot name the kernel `BSplineSurface<Vector4>` carrier (the crate's single sanctioned edge exposes no geometry types) and therefore cannot build the kernel's general `construct::loft` surface. For a two-station loft the smooth station interpolation is exactly determined by the recorded data (linear), so the arm certifies the smooth surface's volume exactly and reproduces the recorded reference. For three or more stations the OCC `ThruSections` station parameterization is not recorded, so certifying any reconstructed surface would be the ruled-substitution / tolerance-stretch the packet forbids. The four loft-stopped corpus rows are all 15-station smooth lofts and therefore refuse typed — the packet's stop condition.
findings.evidence: the smoke above; the four named tests.

stop_conditions.smooth_volume_uncertifiable: FIRED for the four corpus rows, as the packet permits: the smooth-surface volume cannot be certified exactly through the landed machinery because the recorded row does not carry OCC's station-interpolation convention, so the typed refusal naming the open carrier is the deliverable. The refusal is expressible typed (`UnsupportedEnvelope(NonCanonicalCarrier)` -> `{"case": "unsupported_envelope", "envelope": "non_canonical_carrier"}`), so no SPEC_GAP.
stop_conditions.verdict_neutral: No landed green row flipped: the analytic line-section ruled arm is the untouched fast path (bit-identical, `line_loft_rows_answer_bit_identically`), no recorded reference was edited, no tolerance was stretched, and no OCC run was made.
